**Comparison of the two traces**

Both traces follow the same core strategy: group "share a slot" clues into fixed triples, use "immediately left" clues to build adjacency blocks, deduce that Maple must hold 1712, then order the blocks and fill remaining attributes. They diverge in how they handle the remaining uncertainties.

Trace 1 explores alternative year assignments for Maple (1713, 1714, 1716) before concluding Maple must be 1712 — these are CYCLEs that open, explore, and prune with contradictions. It then branches on whether Ash or Cedar holds 1713 (Case A vs Case B), with Case A explored in detail and eliminated. Trace 1 also re-checks the Case A elimination later, a clear LOOP.

Trace 2 is more systematic: it tests all six block permutations and eliminates five, with the longer C-A-B exploration qualifying as a CYCLE. It also re-verifies the 1712 placement deduction and the binding assignments, both LOOPs.

Neither trace contains MUSE episodes — all reasoning stays grounded in the puzzle constraints.

**Annotations**

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="If Maple was 1714: Then 1714 is left of Cedar." end="So Maple cannot be 1714." basis=Opens an alternative year assignment for Maple, works through ordering and constraint implications, and eliminates it when 1712/Ash is not immediately left of Cedar. Payoff is the conclusion that Maple is not 1714.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="If Maple was 1716." end="So Maple cannot be 1716." basis=Opens an alternative where Maple is 1716, derives a contradiction with the Ash-Maple adjacency, and eliminates the branch. Short but complete explore→prune cycle.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="If Maple was 1713." end="Contradiction." basis=Opens an alternative where Maple is 1713, finds that Maple would need both Vellum and Linen bindings, and eliminates it. Very short but complete branch.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case A: Ash is 1713 (Vellum)." end="So Case A2 fails." basis=Opens the branch where Ash holds 1713, explores two subcases for Rag/Cloth binding assignment, both eliminated by the Holly-left-of-Linen constraint. Payoff is the conclusion that Cedar must be 1713.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Order: B3, B1, B2." end="So B3 cannot be first." basis=Opens an alternative block ordering (Holly first), checks Rag-left-of-Holly, finds it impossible since no slot exists left of Holly. Eliminates the order.⟧
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Is there any reason Cedar cannot be 1713?" end="So Ash cannot be 1713." basis=Explicitly re-checks the Case A elimination already completed above. The phrase "I derived it by eliminating Ash=1713. Let's re-check that logic." confirms this is re-execution of a prior step with no new information.⟧
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's re-verify the "Rag left of Holly" constraint." end="Cloth < Maple (Slot 5). 4 < 5. OK." basis=Re-derives Elm=Rag and Ash=Cloth in the B1-B3-B2 order, which was already derived in the "Order 1" section. Adds no new constraint.⟧
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's double check the binding of Elm." end="This is consistent." basis=Re-derives Elm=Rag a third time, confirming a binding assignment already established twice. No new information.⟧

⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Wait, did I check if 1712 could be in Ash?" end="Yes, this was the only option." basis=Re-executes the systematic elimination of 1712 candidates already completed in Step 3. Goes through each label again, reaches the same conclusion that Maple must hold 1712.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="3. C, A, B." end="So C, A, B is invalid." basis=Opens the C-A-B block ordering, checks multiple constraints including year placement and Rag-left-of-Holly, eliminates it when Rag cannot be left of Holly at slot 1.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="4. C, B, A." end="Invalid." basis=Opens the C-B-A block ordering, checks Holly-left-of-Maple and Rag-left-of-Holly, eliminates it when Rag cannot be left of Holly at slot 1.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Let's check B, A, C." end="So invalid." basis=Opens the B-A-C block ordering, checks Holly-left-of-Maple, eliminates it when Holly at slot 6 is not left of Maple at slot 2.⟧
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="5. B, C, A." end="Invalid." basis=Opens the B-C-A block ordering, checks Holly-left-of-Maple, eliminates it when Holly at slot 4 is not left of Maple at slot 2.⟧
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Is it possible for Cloth to be in Slot 2 or 3?" end="So 1713 must be in 6 (with Vellum)." basis=Re-derives binding and year assignments already established in Step 4. Works through Cloth, Rag, 1716, and 1713 placements, reaching identical conclusions.⟧
